problem: Social navigation methods focus on reactive collision avoidance and trajectory adaptation and cannot proactively gather information from humans. As a result, finding a specific person among several residents falls back on exhaustive search.
motivation: Assistive robots in homes or care facilities must find specific individuals among several residents, and people naturally ask others for spatial cues. Communication cues are sparse, heterogeneous and intermittent, so naively adding them to an RL policy does not help (DDPPO with interaction stays at ES 0.14).
key_idea: Pre-train a communication module (COMM) on a proxy task of regressing the target's position from bystander messages, then plug its estimate into a DDPPO navigation policy as a PointGoal-like sensor, so the robot asks non-target humans for cues.
insight: Naively training DDPPO with interaction gives no gain (ES 0.14), and training COMM end-to-end from step 0 reaches only ES 0.18. Pre-training COMM and then fine-tuning the policy reaches ES 0.24, and the appendix longer-training ablation shows the gain comes from the module design, not from extra steps. The language variants perform close to the structured one, and target-prediction error is nearly identical for LLM-generated and human colloquial instructions. Component ablations show that the have-seen flag x_h, recency x_t and the speaker path x_p matter most.
method: CommNav task: the robot queries non-target humans within its field of view and receives a state message S = {x_h have-seen, x_t steps since last seen, x_l last location, x_d direction, x_p 100-point speaker path}, all in egocentric coordinates.

COMM module: a Trajectory Encoder (Spatio-Temporal MLP, 3 heads, H=64) embeds x_p and is concatenated with [x_h, x_t, x_l, x_d]. A 4-layer MLP regressor then outputs the estimated target position, which is fed to the policy as a PointGoal-style sensor; a placeholder is used when no message is available.

Pretext pre-training: 2.4M communication instances collected over 60M steps of baseline training, regressing the ground-truth target location. The policy is then fine-tuned with the frozen COMM (200M+70M steps).

COMM_L language variant: QWEN3-8B verbalizes S into utterances without place names (7000 samples), and a frozen BERT encoder regresses the target location. COMM_L(Human) is evaluated on colloquial instructions from a 20-participant human study.

Habitat 3.0c: a multi-human extension of Habitat 3.0 with ORCA collision avoidance, a probability p=0.25 that humans ignore the robot for the whole episode, and communication triggered at encounters. The policy takes depth and a humanoid detector and outputs linear and angular velocity.
Navigation policy: DDPPO with ResNet visual encoder and RNN, fusing visual features with the COMM estimate. The learned rewards are success- and efficiency-based.

setting.backbone: DDPPO (ResNet + RNN policy, trained with RL) + COMM module (Spatio-Temporal MLP + MLP regressor); language variant uses Qwen3-8B for verbalization and frozen BERT
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat 3.0c for 200M steps (+70M fine-tuning); COMM pre-trained on 2.4M communication instances from 60M sim steps; 7000 Qwen3-8B-verbalized samples for the language variant
setting.observation: egocentric depth + humanoid detector (+ GPS) + structured or language communication message
setting.action_space: continuous linear and angular velocity commands
setting.privileged: Oracle person detection and identification and noiseless sensing in simulation; the messages come from the simulator's ground-truth human state (target location, direction, trajectories)

numbers_note: The benchmark is the paper's own Habitat 3.0c CommNav task, not a canonical benchmark. Full-speed three-human COMM: S 0.67, S_steps 649, SPS 0.35, F 0.09, CR 0.73, CR_T 0.25, ES 0.12.
results: COMM reaches ES 0.24 vs 0.14 for DDPPO with interaction (a 10 pp gain) and 0.16 for SDA, with Finding Success 0.78 vs 0.70 and collision rate 0.51 vs 0.68. Language variants remain close: COMM_L ES 0.20 and COMM_L(Human) ES 0.23. The gains hold and widen with three humans at half speed (ES 0.29 vs 0.24 for SDA).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation with noiseless sensing and oracle person detection/identification; no real robot.
Single-turn interaction only, with no multi-turn dialogue, and messages avoid semantic place names.
The human-study evaluation is small (100 episodes) with high variance (S 0.72±0.05), and the SPS metric slightly decreases due to query detours.
